ranked_monetization_opportunities.title: Fixed-fee B2B pricing-page localization pilot

ranked_monetization_opportunities.six_month_upside: $3k-$20k total if 3-10 pilots close and 2-5 convert into a lightweight hosted subscription or maintenance retainer.
ranked_monetization_opportunities.complexity: Medium. Commercial workflow and tenant-safe runtime are missing, but first pilots can be manually serviced.

ranked_monetization_opportunities.title: Managed hosted pricing-page local-currency widget
ranked_monetization_opportunities.fit: Good 6-month path after pilots. The inline runtime is already embeddable in package form, but it lacks hosted tenant config, signed manifests, billing, customer auth, and operational monitoring.

six_month_revenue_outlook.summary: The realistic six-month path is not a self-serve consumer extension business. It is a service-led B2B wedge that sells pricing-page local-currency demos first, learns from paid pilots, then productizes the repeated pieces into a hosted widget/control-plane if buyers prove the pain.
six_month_revenue_outlook.base_case: $1k-$7k total revenue from 1-5 fixed-fee pilots or audits; small or zero MRR by month six if productization lags.
six_month_revenue_outlook.upside_case: $10k-$30k total revenue plus $500-$3k MRR if outbound closes several SaaS/e-commerce pricing-page pilots and 2-5 convert into hosted monthly support/widget plans.
six_month_revenue_outlook.downside_case: $0 if the project keeps polishing the extension, avoids outbound, or builds SaaS infrastructure before buyer proof.
required_truths: At least one target segment cares enough about pricing-page local-currency hints to pay for a pilot.
A simple additive hint does not create legal/checkout/support problems for the buyer.
Outbound demos produce replies because they are personalized to the prospect page.
Runtime reliability on pricing pages is high enough to avoid embarrassing buyer demos.

positive_revenue_factors: Working browser extension runtime with all-URLs activation shim and bounded scanning; the product already solves a real page-layer problem.
Dependency-free currency parser with locale-aware magnitude handling and configurable symbols/words/ISO codes.
Shared inline runtime package with embeddable ESM/global exports and site plugin architecture.
Existing site-specific plugin work for Amazon and Little Hotelier proves the code can handle messy structured pricing pages.
Local admin/settings workbench already models domain and exact-page overrides, target currency, display style and highlight controls.
B2B landing page and playground already exist, so a pilot page can be productionized faster than starting from zero.
Release, CI, asset optimization and marketplace publishing scripts are stronger than most zero-revenue side projects.
Privacy posture is credible: extension CSP and host permissions are narrow for rate providers, and Firefox manifest declares no required data collection.
AI-assisted coding/design can compress landing page cleanup, demo creation, plugin adaptation and reporting into days rather than weeks.
negative_revenue_factors: There is no visible revenue system: no billing, checkout, pricing plans, paid entitlements, license checks, customer accounts or CRM.
The website is not production-ready: placeholder domain, placeholder email, placeholder canonical/OG/sitemap URLs, and no real lead capture.
No analytics or funnel measurement exists for website visits, demo clicks, extension activation, retention, uninstall, outbound response or conversion.
Current backend/admin is local-only tooling, not a SaaS control plane: it binds to 127.0.0.1, uses local SQLite and can trigger local extension builds.
The marketplace/review moat is effectively zero; FX Inline has no meaningful public user proof yet.
Consumer currency conversion is crowded and mostly free; strong competitors already own generic extension search terms.
Client-side public rate providers are fine for a free extension but weak for a paid B2B promise unless rate freshness, fallback and disclaimers are explicit.
The extension has broad page access by nature, so trust copy, privacy disclosure and support responsiveness must be unusually clear.
Technical polishing that does not create buyer learning, trust, distribution or paid conversion is a distraction right now.

positive: Users like conversion without leaving the page: hover, right-click, inline, popup, or overlay all reduce context switching.
Original-price visibility matters; users want conversion context without losing the source price.
Site-specific controls, quick on/off toggles and per-site disablement recur as useful features.
Clean lightweight UI is praised more than feature depth when the job is simple.
Privacy/no tracking/no strange permissions is an explicit trust signal in new entrant launches and marketplace listings.
For merchants, support and onboarding are revenue features, not overhead. MLV reviews repeatedly mention responsive support as the reason setup worked.
negative: Wrong values, stale rates, aggressive rounding and ambiguous symbols damage trust immediately.
Confusing settings are a recurring complaint for mature extensions.
Extensions that stop working on dynamic pages or after browser updates get punished in reviews.
CPU/memory overload on complex sites is a real risk for all-page conversion tools.
Intrusive rating prompts are called out and can create ethical/trust concerns.
Currency coverage gaps produce feature requests and bad reviews, especially for non-US/non-EU users.
feature_requests: Per-site disablement and site currency override
More currencies and better ambiguous-symbol handling
Cached/offline rates and clear last-updated timestamp
Hover mode plus inline mode plus context-menu fallback
Original value shown beside converted value
Readable highlights and less intrusive UI
Better options search and currency selection
trust_concerns: All-sites permissions create perceived risk even when necessary.
Rate accuracy and source credibility must be visible.
Any merchant-facing pricing hint must avoid implying checkout-final pricing unless checkout is integrated.
Analytics must be privacy-scoped and disclosed clearly; the current extension posture is data-collection-minimal.
revenue_relevant_insights: Consumer extension users value the tool but have many free options, so consumer premium is a poor first-dollar path.
Merchant reviews show willingness to pay when localization is tied to international sales, setup and support.
The best B2B language is not “currency converter”; it is “reduce buyer confusion and improve international pricing confidence.”
Support quality can be packaged into a paid pilot because buyers need help integrating localized pricing safely.

ai_execution_assumptions_used.design: AI design tools can quickly create landing-page visuals, before/after screenshots, demo videos, store screenshots and outreach creative. The bottleneck is choosing a credible offer and target audience.
